title: The Civil answer to the charge
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：civil　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 civil 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the fisherman wrote of ① a civil answer to the charge in the logbook, and everybody in the harbour said at once that it was ② so civil that nobody in the harbour would go near it. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the fisherman, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the civil ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the civil answer to the charge that anybody there had ever seen, or so the logbook for July 1955 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too civil to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the boatman who had come to help; the civil ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a civil case in the court, and said that no boatman in his right mind would call it ⑥ as civil as the case in the court they had once had in the old harbour. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was civil or not, and he said so.

By 1968 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the logbook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something civil, and nothing besides. The boatman from the next harbour called the whole plan ⑧ quite civil; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the logbook kept the names of the civil ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1971, in the rain, she wrote of another civil answer to the charge in the same logbook, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ no less civil than anybody had expected. ⑩ The civil case in the court that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1973, was the one she could never quite name; the civil ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 文明（前置定语 a civil answer to the charge：1961 年渔人在航海日志里记下的那件文明的答辩）
B. adj. 文明／民事（两处加强说法：so civil that … 与 no less civil than …）
C. adj. 文明／民事（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 文明（表语 too civil to do：母亲觉得它太文明，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 民事（前置定语 a civil case in the court：叔叔把整件事称作一桩民事的案子）
F. adj. 民事（同级比较 as civil as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩法庭上的案子相比）
G. adj. 民事（后置定语 something civil：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 民事（受程度副词修饰 quite civil：那位船工的评价）

items.q: a civil answer to the charge
the civil answer to the charge that
a civil case in the court
The civil case in the court that

answers.why: civil 意为“文明”，1961 年渔人在航海日志里记下的是“一件文明的答辩”，此处作前置定语 a civil answer to the charge。
civil 意为“文明”，此处用 so civil that 结构，说它文明到渔港里没人敢靠近。
civil 意为“文明”，航海日志上 七月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的文明对指控的答辩，等于最高级的说法。
civil 意为“文明”，母亲认为这件东西“太文明了，谁也用不上”，too civil to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
civil 意为“民事”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩民事的案子”，此处作前置定语 a civil case in the court。
civil 意为“民事”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩法庭上的案子一样民事”，同级比较用 as civil as。
civil 意为“民事”，航海日志上那半行字要的是“民事的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something civil。
civil 意为“民事”，邻渔港来的那位船工认为这套计划“相当民事”，quite 修饰原级 civil。
civil 意为“民事”，no less civil than 表示“其民事不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之民事不亚于任何人的预料。
civil 意为“民事”，母亲 1973 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的民事案子”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1961 年，渔人在航海日志里记下了一件文明的答辩。（a civil answer to the charge）
它文明到渔港里没有一个人敢靠近。（so civil that …）
母亲觉得它太文明，谁也用不上。（too civil to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩民事的案子。（a civil case in the court）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩法庭上的案子一样民事。（as civil as …）
到了 1968 年，航海日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件民事的东西。（something civil）
answers: In 1961 the fisherman wrote of a civil answer to the charge in the logbook.
It was so civil that nobody in the harbour would go near it.
My mother thought it too civil to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a civil case in the court.
He said nobody would call it as civil as the case in the court they had once had.
By 1968 the logbook asked for nothing but something civil.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 civil 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the fisherman wrote of a civil answer to the charge in the logbook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the civil answer to the charge that anybody there had ever seen, or so the logbook says.
My mother thought it too civil to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a civil case in the court, and nobody argued with him.
The boatman from the next harbour called the plan quite civil, and everybody laughed.
The civil ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
